accuracy.reason: Cards 1-4 accurately separate key-value access from cache/durability role, replacement from merge, confirmed absence from timeout, namespaces from permission, and known-key reads from maintained search paths. Cards 5-9 preserve atomicity/repetition, lifetime, partition/read/durability and workload-fit boundaries.

evidence.quote: Start with what the caller knows: the key, and which value it needs.

mechanisms.reason: Lost-update arithmetic motivates an indivisible version condition and write, reread/recompute on rejection and bounded retry. Unknown write outcome, intervening writers and durable operation/effect coordination explain duplicate safety. TTL/eviction and hot-key/lagging-reader cases expose distinct failure mechanisms.

evidence.quote: Know the operation's semantics before interpreting its result.

coherence.reason: API records, overlapping requests and missing network responses are explicit prerequisites. Nine cards build model, operations, identity/value design, query needs, concurrency, retry, lifetime, distribution and selection. Inspected namespace diagram denies permission from keys; version diagram correctly rejects stale version4 then recomputes12. Shared renderer/CSS inspected earlier, not executed.

evidence.quote: Design identity, value boundaries and authorization as separate decisions.

decisions.reason: Value size, key encoding, authorization, index maintenance/visibility, conditional-write scope, retry-window deduplication, required-data retention and hot-key capacity are concrete checks. Card9 compares independent known-key fit against scans/indexes/joins and richer alternatives with measurement, not universal speed/safety.

evidence.quote: List the questions your application must answer before choosing its keys and indexes.

clarity.reason: Each term is defined through behavior: absent versus empty, full replacement removing color, unambiguous tenant identity, scan work, atomic version test, expiry visibility and durability versus read consistency. Brief examples expose the relevant gap without prescribing unsupported product capabilities.

evidence.quote: The condition and the write must share the same atomic boundary.

outcomes.reason: Learner uses tenant/device/record-kind with forbidden-or-escaped separator and complete settings value, distinguishes authoritative source from disposable cache and configured durability, traces replacement to mode:loud then deletion absence, keeps get timeout unknown and checks tenant/record permission separately.

Learner explains missing known IDs for region query, scan work despite filtering, alternate region-to-ID index with fetches, storage/update/deletion maintenance and visibility responsibility, and verifies selected product support rather than assuming it.

Learner computes blind final21 instead of22, allows only one version7 conditional success with version advancement, rereads21/current version and recomputes22 for a bounded conditional retry. It correctly rejects separate check/unconditional put and limits atomic scope.

Learner leaves timed-out effect unknown, distinguishes repeat-identical replacement under no intervening write from double increment, requires verified stable intent/ID plus atomic retained duplicate record or recovery without blind retry. It separates TTL and capacity eviction, denies retention/refresh/scheduling guarantees and checks expiry visibility/configuration.

Learner defines partition/keyspace assignment, many-key distribution versus concentrated hot-key capacity, lag-permitted read visibility and distinct acknowledged-write failure survival, requiring actual modes, replication and persistence guarantees rather than label/node count.

Learner selects known-key independent A fit and explains B scan/index/application-join work, chooses atomic concurrent update and authoritative durability checks with reasons, and denies universal speed/safety while retaining representative load/failure measurement and other required guarantees.

sourceChecks.claim: Live DynamoDB core components reference confirms unique primary keys identify structured items; the lesson treats authority, caching and durability as separate requirements rather than universal product-label properties.

Live GetItem reference distinguishes absent Item from returned attributes and read mode; official PutItem followup confirms complete replacement and permitted empty non-key values. A failed request cannot establish absence.

Live fine-grained IAM reference requires identity-based item/attribute permissions, supporting separate authorization from namespaced identity. Key encoding and value grouping are reasoned application choices, not claimed automatic service features.

Live secondary-index reference supplies alternate lookup keys, storage/update capacity and differing consistency modes; official Scan followup confirms filters do not reduce already consumed read work.

Live condition-expression examples reject updates when their conditions fail; official optimistic-locking followup confirms client/server version mismatch failure and version advancement, with product scope caveats consistent with the lesson.

Live DynamoDB error guide explicitly says failed-response writes may have succeeded or failed and recommends conditions or idempotent transaction tokens. Previously inspected AWS idempotency guidance supports atomic token/effect recording; retry and retention scope remain explicit checks.

Live DynamoDB TTL reference says expired items await background deletion and may need filtering, supporting expiry-visibility and no exact-time action claims. Previously inspected Redis eviction reference supports capacity removal as a separately configured mechanism.

Live partition-key guidance calls for uniform key activity and per-partition/value-size throughput limits; previously inspected DynamoDB read-consistency and current GetItem references support mode-dependent stale reads. Durability is correctly separated and must be verified.

Live DynamoDB NoSQL design guidance emphasizes limited efficient access patterns versus relational flexibility and designing around application needs. Lesson preserves actual richer product support and measures workload/correctness rather than inferring performance from the label.
